correctness.rationale: The defining two coprimality exclusions and parity give the uniform bound \(\lvert2T(n)-nb(n)\rvert\le3^{\omega(n)}\) with exact equality for \(4\mid n\); direct rational finite checks cover \(n\le1200\). CRT supplies independence of finite divisibility indicators; the omitted prime tail averages at most \(\sum_{p>y}p^{-2}\); the arithmetic error has Cesaro L1 bound \(O((\log x)^3/x)\). The random product is almost surely positive by summable expected logarithms, and finite products are injective by the largest differing prime denominator. Independence plus divergent \(\sum_p1/p\) proves no atoms, and computes all fixed moments. The squarefree Dirichlet convolution h=b*mu and divisor-function summation prove the \(x^2\) main term with \(O(x(\log x)^2)\) error. A separate exact finite-product injection test of 512 products passed. This is an infinite proof independent of finite experiments.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Renshaw pointwise estimates together with standard probabilistic number theory could imply a route to the present theorem, but the source does not claim or prove the infinite distribution, absence of atoms or explicit moment sequence. The earlier phi_2 summatory formula cannot be substituted at \(p=2\): it gives identically zero even terms versus \(b(2^a)=1/2\). Our summatory constant is consequently distinct, and the new primary mathematical contribution is the explicit atomless limit law, not the reuse of classical independence tools.

originality.rationale: Renshaw (2026) introduces the nonmultiplicative totient and pointwise formula/bounds but not its limiting probability law or atomlessness. Steuding and Suriajaya (2023) sum the multiplicative generalized Schemmel function, which differs from \(T(n)\) and its normalized surrogate at the prime 2; their main theorem does not imply an atomless limit law for T. Delange/Wintner-style generic multiplicative-distribution principles could streamline the existence argument but cannot be equated with a prior explicit theorem on this object. Actual semantic record searches and exact-statement web searches returned no covering finding; they are not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: A general earlier distribution theorem for multiplicative functions might imply the surrogate b(n) result after combining it with Renshaw pointwise bounds, even if it has no matching notation.
An inaccessible or unindexed prior theorem could already contain an equivalent atomlessness argument.
The related 2015 source was assessed by abstract only.

value.rationale: The natural variant totient is tied to counting spurious candidates in semigroup-variant arithmetic and was previously treated pointwise. This theorem characterizes its normalized typical values by a non-atomic, positive, explicit Euler-product law, all fixed moments, and a sharp main-order global summation with quantified remainder. The atomlessness is structurally non-obvious, since zero occurs for some finite n and several nearby Schemmel ratios have an atom at zero. This is a motivated complete distributional classification at fixed normalization, not an isolated computation or arbitrary finite slice.
